thread:
amy (sales): quick sync — MerchantOnramp (large fintech) wants a POC leading to a committed reserved pool. They sent the security questionnaire and a traffic profile. asking for: reserved GPU sizing, autoscale fallback, preheat plan, and a price delta for reserved vs burst. can we triage?

devin (solutions): on it. sharing the traffic sample — looks spiky with daily peak windows. rough numbers in the questionnaire: 150 qps sustained during peak 2-3 hours, 600 qps short bursts (1-5m), average token length ~400.

jay (eng-infra): thanks. for 150 sustained qps with 400 tokens, assuming batch-friendly chat model, estimate ~2x rtx6000-equivalents for reserved to hit <200ms p95. bursts to 600 qps => need burst pool or autoscale to add ~3 extra instances. prefer reserved + burst credits.

kevin (security): flagged HIPAA and customer-managed KMS. questionnaire asks about HSM integration and audit log retention (7 years). Private deployment acceptable? Merchant prefers VPC with our private plane.

olivia (cs): timeline: they want commitment by EoQ if POC looks good. we need a clear runbook to show zero-downtime fallbacks. also they asked about SSO + SCIM for onboarding.

devin (solutions): attaching simplified traffic snippet for sizing discussion:

```json
{
  "window": "weekday peaks",
  "sustained_qps": 150,
  "burst_qps": 600,
  "median_tokens": 400,
  "burst_duration": "1-5m",
  "concurrency_model": "chat-heavy"
}
```

jay (eng-infra): quick notes:
- preheat KV cache for top 20 prefixes with small warm-up job.
- autoscale policy: cooldown 60s, add nodes in batches of 2, max burst pool sized for 4 instances.
- queue depth limit: apply backpressure at 1200 in-flight requests to avoid OOMs.

amy (sales): can you sketch cost delta? they asked for reserved price vs pay-as-you-go with burst credits.

jay (eng-infra): rough back-of-envelope: reserved pool (2 GPUs) + 4 burst credits for peak runway -> ~monthly reserved delta = $X (we'll produce exact with finance), PAYG peak costs ~1.6x higher during heavy bursts. I'll ping finance for a formal quote.

kevin (security): for questionnaire: confirm KMS/HSM support, VPC peering, audit logs exported to their SIEM (syslog/S3), and we can offer 7-year retention add-on. mark me to review final answers.

olivia (cs): POC acceptance criteria request: 1) p95 latency <300ms for sustained load, 2) no data exfil on logs, 3) failover to lower-cap model within 30s on eviction, 4) successful SSO test.

devin (solutions): propose POC config:
- Dedicated reserved pool: 2 GPUs (baseline)
- Burst pool / credits: capacity to add up to 4 GPUs for 10m/day average
- Autoscale rules: scale-up threshold at 70% GPU util, scale-down 30% util with cooldown 60s
- KV preheat: scripted warm-up job run 15m before expected peak windows

amy (sales): love it. next steps?

jay (eng-infra): I can draft the preheat + autoscale runbook and a short ops checklist for failures (node eviction, AZ loss). will include SLOs and rollback policy. estimated draft by EOD tomorrow.

kevin (security): I'll start filling the questionnaire answers and map the HSM/KMS notes to our compliance doc. need an architecture diagram for on-prem/pipelines.

olivia (cs): I'll confirm onboarding dates with MerchantOnramp and request their SIEM endpoint and SSO contact.

amy (sales): assign action items: @devin final POC config + sample prompts, @jay ops runbook + cost delta draft, @kevin sec questionnaire, @olivia customer coordination. I'll prepare a short one-pager for legal/finance.

deploy-bot: Deployment window scheduled: staging preheat job run at 2025-06-04T14:45Z (auto-created).

devin (solutions): ping @jay — do we want to add quantized model variant for burst to save cost? 8-bit should be compatible; minor quality delta.

jay (eng-infra): yes — suggest two-tier model plan: baseline FP16, burst 8-bit quantized fallback. router policy: prefer baseline, fall back to quantized when queue depth > 900 or when CPU/GPU memory constrained.

amy (sales): perfect. I'll send MerchantOnramp the POC plan and security checklist tonight. keep thread updated with the docs/links.

kevin (security): noted. will review before you send.

olivia (cs): thanks team. short check-in tomorrow 10am PT?

amy (sales): 10am works. :white_check_mark:
